{"title":"Overview & Quick Start","description":"Wearables platform overview","visualizations":{"ov_md":{"type":"splunk.markdown","options":{"markdown":"# Wearables Health

Vendor-neutral health dashboards on the **Wearables data model** — one set of panels
that work across devices (**Oura**, **Garmin**, and **Withings**).

## Quick start
1. **Create the `wearables` index and set up HEC** — both are required before any data can land:
 - **Index:** Settings → Indexes → New Index → `wearables` (Events). On Cloud, use the console / ACS.
 - **HEC token:** Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → enable it, then **New Token** with its allowed/default index set to `wearables`. Note the endpoint: `https://<host>:8088/services/collector/event` (Enterprise) or `https://http-inputs-<stack>.splunkcloud.com:443/...` (Cloud — port **443**, real cert). You'll put this URL + token in the fetcher's targets file.
2. Install + restart Splunk:
 - **TA-oura** (Oura) — plus **TA-garmin** (Garmin) and **TA-withings** (Withings scale).
 - **wearables** — this app (data model + dashboards).
 - **hypnogram_viz** + **charge_ring_viz** — custom visualizations used by the dashboards.
3. Run the vendor ingest (repo-only tooling — needs a Splunk HEC token; never shipped in the app):
 - **Oura:** `oura_to_hec_with_phi.py` (OAuth token → HEC `index=wearables`).
 - **Garmin:** `garmin_to_hec.py` (Path B via `python-garminconnect`) — see TA-garmin's `INSTALL.md`.
 - **Withings:** `withings_to_hec.py` (OAuth2 → HEC) — body weight & composition; see TA-withings's `INSTALL.md`.
4. Populate the admin KV registries via **Admin → People & Defaults**: **`wearable_person_profile`**
 (`person_id` → name / default units / goals / height / **birth month** (age) / Splunk-login map / **household**); device names via **`wearable_device_profile`**; family caregiver→dependent edges via **`wearable_relationships`**.
5. Open the dashboards: **Today · Family · Family Graph · Sleep · Heart · Activity · Wellness · Device**.

## How it fits together
- **Per-vendor add-ons** (`TA-oura`, `TA-garmin`, `TA-withings`, …) ingest each device's data and normalize it
 into canonical fields (`total_sleep_min`, `avg_hr`, `steps`, …) + vendor-neutral tags.
- The **Wearables data model** (Sleep / HeartRate / Activity / Workout / Daily / Device) exposes
 those canonical fields — the dashboards read **only** the model, so a new vendor just works.
- **Ingest scripts live in each vendor add-on's `tools/`** (repo-only, excluded from the `.spl`
 since they hold credentials).

## Access & identity
- Every event carries an indexed **`person_id`** (opaque) + **`vendor`**, stamped at ingest.
- Per-person isolation is enforced by role **`srchFilter`** on `person_id` (RBAC).
- Names / goals / device names come from admin-managed KV lookups (never the access gate).
- **Family view** — the **Family** page lists a household's members from the People registry (so a member shows even before any device data arrives), with a **Household** picker; metric *values* still obey per-person RBAC (`srchFilter` on `person_id`). Caregiver access itself comes from *role composition* — assigning a viewer each family member's per-person role OR's their `srchFilter`s into that family's set. The `wearable_relationships` KV records the caregiver→dependent edges that drive those assignments (enrichment, not the gate) — edit them in **Admin → Relationships**, visualize them on **Family Graph**.

## Privacy — PII / PHI
- **No strong PII in the registry.** `wearable_person_profile` (KV Store) holds only low-sensitivity enrichment — display name, goals, units, height, `splunk_user` (login map), and **`birth_ym` (birth month + year only, `YYYY-MM` — never the day)**. Age is computed at search time; month+year keeps it accurate all year except within the birth month and is **not** fraud-grade PII (a full DOB is). Never store a full DOB, SSN, address, or email-as-data.
- **The KV registry is collection-readable, not row-scoped.** `inputlookup` returns *every* person's row to anyone who can run it (writes are admin-only) — shared enrichment, which is why nothing sensitive lives there. True per-row isolation needs a mediated REST handler (roadmap).
- **The real access boundary is index RBAC.** All health data lives in `index=wearables`, keyed by an **opaque `person_id`** (a surrogate key, not a name); per-person isolation is a role **`srchFilter`** on `person_id`. This only protects data **where those roles are configured** — until then the temporary Person picker shows all data to all users.
- **Nothing sensitive ships in a package.** Every `.spl` passes an automated PII/secret scan before release; only synthetic (`synthetic="true"`) sample data is included.

## Repositories
- **Wearables app** (this): [github.com/narwhaldc/wearables](https://github.com/narwhaldc/wearables)
- **Oura add-on** — TA-oura: [github.com/narwhaldc/TA-oura](https://github.com/narwhaldc/TA-oura)
- **Garmin add-on** — TA-garmin: [github.com/narwhaldc/TA-garmin](https://github.com/narwhaldc/TA-garmin)
- **Withings add-on** — TA-withings: [github.com/narwhaldc/TA-withings](https://github.com/narwhaldc/TA-withings)
- **Hypnogram viz**: [github.com/narwhaldc/hypnogram_viz](https://github.com/narwhaldc/hypnogram_viz)
- **Charge / Ring viz**: [github.com/narwhaldc/charge_ring_viz](https://github.com/narwhaldc/charge_ring_viz)
- **Legacy single-vendor app** — oura_health: [github.com/narwhaldc/oura-health-splunk](https://github.com/narwhaldc/oura-health-splunk)

## Status
First-pass quick start. Dashboards are migrating off the single-vendor **oura_health** app
(the GA fallback). Requires `index=wearables`, `TA-oura`, and person_id-based RBAC.

## Scope & known limitations
- **Data timing follows each vendor's API, not the wall clock.** Oura, Garmin, and Withings all backdate and later revise data — a night's sleep isn't written until you wake and sync, and readings for prior days can be inserted or updated hours later. The most recent day or two can be incomplete or shift as vendors fill them in; dashboards are only as current as both the last ingest run and each vendor's own timing.
- **Max HR and training zones are estimates, not measured.** Heart-rate zones use the Tanaka formula (208 − 0.7 × age) personalized with your resting HR (Karvonen), not a measured maximum. A true personal max needs a max-effort test; an observed peak usually underestimates it.
- **Implausible heart-rate spikes are filtered.** The Oura normalization drops readings above a plausible physiological ceiling (> 200 bpm) as PPG sensor artifacts, so peaks and averages reflect real beats.
- **Walk Equivalent vs Distance are different metrics.** Oura reports an energy-derived *equivalent* walking distance (**Walk Equivalent**); Garmin reports *literal* distance travelled (**Distance**). They show in separate tiles — a person with both devices sees both.
- **Some Oura metrics need extra API scopes.** Cardiovascular Age and Resilience exist in the Oura API but require additional scopes on your token; without them those tiles stay empty.
- **Vendor coverage varies.** Not every metric exists on every device, so vendor-specific panels appear only when that person has that vendor's data (e.g. body composition from Withings, some Garmin-only metrics).
- **Today's Recovery tile adapts to your device.** It leads with Oura **Readiness Score** when you have an Oura ring, otherwise Garmin **Body Battery** — both 0–100 recovery indices — so the daily snapshot always shows a recovery metric when either vendor provides one.
